value.body: Metallurgical and Materials Engineering covers how metals and other materials are extracted, processed, shaped, tested and chosen: physical and mechanical metallurgy, iron and steelmaking, phase transformations, heat treatment, corrosion, welding, casting and characterisation. Some institutes call it Materials Science and Engineering. It leads to steel and non-ferrous plants, foundries and forging, automotive and aerospace suppliers, testing labs and research.

items.note: 8 semesters; diploma holders can join year 2 through lateral entry

value.title: How you get in
value.body: You choose the branch at counselling, after the entrance exam. JEE Advanced rank is used for IITs; JEE Main rank for NITs, IIITs and other centrally funded institutes — all allotted through JoSAA. State colleges use state counselling with a state CET (EAMCET, MHT-CET, KCET, WBJEE and others) or, in Tamil Nadu (TNEA), Class 12 marks. Class 12 with Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics is required. The branch is offered mainly at IITs, NITs and some state and private colleges.

value.title: At a glance
items: Steel and metal plants are large employers; much of the work is at plant sites in mineral belts and industrial towns.
GATE (MT paper) is used for M.Tech admissions and by some steel and mineral PSUs; BARC and DRDO also recruit metallurgists.
Research and advanced-materials roles (aerospace, nuclear, defence labs) often expect an M.Tech or PhD.
UPSC ESE has no Metallurgy stream.
